item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Tshisekedi’s 2024 record is mixed, but the balance leans against a strong “evidence and correction” reading. There is real evidence of IMF-backed, technocratic macro management and some administrative coordination. But the stronger pattern is still opaque public finance, slow corrective follow-through, weak institutional accountability, and occasional scapegoating/blame-shifting instead of plain ownership of mistakes.

**Accepted Claims**
- [IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement with the Democratic Republic of Congo on an Extended Credit Facility and a Resilience and Sustainability Facility](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/11/13/pr-24416-drc-imf-reaches-agreement-on-ecf-and-rsf) | IMF | 2024-11-13 | The IMF said the new program was built around inclusive growth, diversification, job creation, governance, transparency, and tighter expenditure-chain discipline. This is the strongest direct evidence that the administration was using evidence-based macro policy tools rather than slogans alone. | `5B.7` `5B.3` `5B.4` `5B.6` `E0343`

- [IMF Executive Board Concludes the 2024 Article IV Consultation and Completes the Sixth Review under the ECF Arrangement](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/03/pr24253-drc-imf-exec-board-concludes-2024-art-iv-consult-completes-6th-rev-ecf-arr) | IMF | 2024-07-03 | The IMF said the authorities kept prudent macro policies, avoided monetary financing, and made progress on revenue mobilization and reserve build-up, while also noting slow reform progress and still-elevated inflation. This supports a cautious positive reading on evidence-based macro management, but not a strong record of rapid correction. | `5B.7` `5B.3` `5B.6` `E0342`

**Bottom Line**
Tshisekedi’s 2024 record is mixed, but it leans negative for 5B.7. There is real evidence of technocratic macro-policy adjustment through the IMF process and some administrative coordination. But the stronger pattern is still opaque administration, weak self-correction, and repeated external blame-shifting or slogan-heavy framing rather than clear evidence-based learning.

**Accepted Claims**

This is the strongest positive evidence for evidence-based economic policy. | `5B.7` `5B.3` `5B.6` `E0342`

- [IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement with the Democratic Republic of Congo on an Extended Credit Facility and a Resilience and Sustainability Facility](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/11/13/pr-24416-drc-imf-reaches-agreement-on-ecf-and-rsf) | IMF | 2024-11-13 | The IMF framed the new program around inclusive growth, diversification, job creation, governance, and tighter expenditure-chain controls, treasury reforms, and lower tax exemptions. That is strong evidence of policy designed through diagnosis and correction rather than pure slogan. | `5B.7` `5B.3` `5B.4` `5B.6` `E0343`

This is limited but real evidence of administrative learning and policy execution. | `5B.7` `5B.3` `5B.6` `E0344`

This is weak positive rhetoric for openness, but it is thin evidence compared with the stronger correction and scapegoating signals elsewhere. | `5B.7` `5B.8` `E0305`

That is lawful pressure, but it also shows a tendency to externalize blame rather than plainly own policy failure. | `5B.7` `5B.5` `5B.1` `E0164`

- [Tshisekedi threatens war against Rwanda, while relying on proxy forces](https://d2233.cms.socastsrm.com/2024/07/04/army-disarray-hobbles-congos-fight-with-rwanda-backed-rebels-officers-say/) | Reuters | 2024-07-04 | Reuters reported that Tshisekedi threatened to declare war against Rwanda while relying on proxy forces. This is the clearest evidence of escalation rhetoric and blame-shifting rather than calm, evidence-based correction. | `5B.7` `5B.1` `5B.5` `E0093` `E0100`

**Search Gap**
I found strong evidence of IMF-driven adjustment and some policy coordination, but little direct proof that Tshisekedi routinely reviewed failed policies, acknowledged errors, or changed course based on measured results outside the macro-fiscal lane. The main missing piece is concrete, repeated evidence of domestic policy correction in sectors like services, procurement, and provincial administration.
